What You Need Before You Start

ItemWhy it is needed
The exact legal corporation nameIt must match the registry record
The nine-digit business numberThe return is filed against it and its RC account
The fiscal year-end on record with the Canada Revenue AgencyA mismatch rejects the transmission
Which tax years are outstandingEach year is a separate return
Any balances on the booksShare capital, cash or a shareholder loan make GIFI schedules required
A signing officer available to signForm T183CORP is signed before transmission

Nothing else is needed for a true nil year. There are no receipts to gather and no statements to prepare, because there was no activity to report.

Confirming the Fiscal Year-End

This is the first step and the one that most often goes wrong. The Canada Revenue Agency already holds a fiscal year-end for the corporation, taken from the incorporation record, and the return must carry that same date.

Owners usually remember the date the business started trading rather than the date on the incorporation record. A year-end that differs from the one the Agency holds rejects the transmission.

The Business Number and RC Account

The return is filed against the nine-digit business number and its RC corporation income tax account. Most corporations receive the number at incorporation.

A corporation that was never registered with the Canada Revenue Agency has to obtain one before anything can be transmitted. See whether a business number is needed to file a nil T2.

Checking the Year Is Actually Nil

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

An expense claimedNo
PayrollNo

Investment or rental incomeNo
A dividend paid or receivedNo
None of the aboveYes

T2 Short or the Full T2

The T2 Short is a two-page version of the return, available to a Canadian-controlled private corporation that meets eight conditions. Most nil years qualify.

Either form is included in the fee. The choice is made from the facts of the year rather than by the corporation, and it changes nothing about the deadline.

The conditions are set out in the guide to T2 Short eligibility.

The GIFI Schedules

A corporation inactive all year with nothing at all to report may omit GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141. Any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes them required.

This is where a return that looks nil is most often filed incorrectly. The detail is in the guide to GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141.

Schedules 24, 50 and 8

ScheduleWhen it is required
Schedule 24On the first return after incorporation
Schedule 50For every shareholder holding 10% or more
Schedule 8Capital cost allowance, recorded with loss continuity

Schedule 8 and the loss continuity that travels with it are covered in the guide to Schedule 8 and loss continuity.

CPA Review Before Transmission

A CPA Ontario member reviews the completed return before it is transmitted: the year-end against the Agency record, the GIFI coding, the schedule selection and the nil status itself.

That review is what the fee buys. A corporation filing on its own with commercial tax software takes on the same checks. See whether a nil T2 can be filed without an accountant.

Signing Form T183CORP

An authorized signing officer signs Form T183CORP before the return is transmitted, never after. It carries a date and an HH:MM:SS timestamp that is never backdated, and may be e-signed through an access-controlled secure portal.

One form is signed per tax year, because each year is a separate return with its own transmission. The form is kept by the firm for six years and is not sent to the Agency unless requested.

The full detail is in the guide to Form T183CORP signing and transmission.

Transmission and CRA Confirmation

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

For tax years starting after 2023, e-filing is mandatory for virtually all corporations, and a paper T2 draws a $1,000.00 penalty plus a $100.00 per-return preparer penalty. Your CRA confirmation is emailed within 3 business days. One corrected transmission is included where the Agency rejects the first.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Filing More Than One Year

Each outstanding year is its own return, with its own fiscal year-end, its own figures and its own T183CORP signature. They are filed oldest first, so the balances carry forward correctly.

Frequently Asked Questions

How Long Does Filing a Nil T2 Take?

The return itself is short, and the usual wait is for the fiscal year-end to be confirmed and for the signing officer to sign Form T183CORP. The CRA confirmation is emailed within 3 business days of transmission.

What Do I Have to Send You?

The legal corporation name, the business number, the fiscal year-end, which years are outstanding, and any balances sitting on the books. For a true nil year there are no receipts and no statements to prepare.

Can I File Without Knowing My Fiscal Year-End?

No. The year-end must match the record the Canada Revenue Agency holds or the transmission is rejected, so it is confirmed before the return is prepared rather than guessed.

Do I Have to Sign Anything?

Yes. An authorized signing officer signs Form T183CORP before the return is transmitted, one for each tax year being filed. It can be e-signed through a secure portal with a single-use link.

What if the CRA Rejects the Return?

One corrected transmission is included in the fee. A rejection is usually a year-end that does not match the Agency record, and it is a filing that has not landed yet rather than a failed one.

Is a Paper T2 Still an Option?

Not in practice. For tax years starting after 2023, e-filing is mandatory for virtually all corporations, and a paper T2 draws a $1,000.00 penalty plus a $100.00 per-return preparer penalty.

meta_description: What GIFI is, what Schedules 100, 125 and 141 report, when a nil return may omit them, and why share capital or a shareholder loan makes them required.
content:
GIFI Guide

The Complete Guide to GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141

What GIFI is, what Schedules 100, 125 and 141 report, when a nil return may omit them, and why share capital or a shareholder loan makes them required. Nil T2 filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What GIFI Is

GIFI stands for the General Index of Financial Information. It is the standard code set the Canada Revenue Agency uses for the balance sheet and the income statement inside the T2.

It exists so that every corporation reports the same item under the same code, whatever its own bookkeeping calls it. A corporation does not file its accountant’s statements; it files the figures mapped onto GIFI codes.

Schedules 100, 125 and 141

ScheduleWhat it reports
Schedule 100The balance sheet: assets, liabilities and equity
Schedule 125The income statement: revenue and expenses
Schedule 141A checklist about who prepared the figures and whether a review or audit was done

The three travel together. A return that files one generally files all three.

Schedule 100, the Balance Sheet

Schedule 100 reports what the corporation owns and owes at the fiscal year-end. On a dormant corporation this is often a single line of share capital and a matching line of cash or a shareholder loan.

A balance sheet does not become nil because the year was nil. Balances sit on the books until something removes them, and they are reported every year they exist.

Schedule 125, the Income Statement

Schedule 125 reports revenue and expenses for the year. On a true nil year this is where the nil actually appears: no revenue, no expenses, nil net income.

A single bank charge is an expense, and a corporation that paid one has something to report on Schedule 125 even though it traded not at all.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Schedule 141, the Notes Checklist

Schedule 141 is a short set of questions about the financial information itself: who prepared it, whether an accountant was involved, and whether the statements were audited, reviewed or neither.

For a nil return the answer is normally that no audit and no review was performed, which is accurate and expected. It is a disclosure rather than a judgement.

When a Nil Return May Omit Them

A corporation that was inactive all year and has nothing at all to report may omit GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141. Nothing at all means no assets, no liabilities, no equity balance, no revenue and no expenses.

That is a narrower case than most owners assume. A corporation with $100.00 of share capital does not meet it.

What Makes Them Required

On the books at the year-endGIFI schedules required
Share capital of any amountYes
Cash in a corporate bank accountYes
A shareholder loan in either directionYes
Incorporation costs capitalisedYes
A bank charge paid during the yearYes
Nothing at allNo

Share Capital and Shareholder Loans

These two are the usual reason a dormant corporation still files GIFI. Share capital was issued when the corporation was set up and has sat on the balance sheet ever since. A shareholder loan is whatever the owner put in or took out.

Neither is income and neither creates tax. They are balances, and a balance is reported because it exists, not because anything happened to it during the year.

The Most Common Nil-Return Error

Omitting the GIFI schedules on a corporation that has balances is the single most common reason a return that looks nil is not filed correctly.

The return goes in, the year looks closed, and the omission surfaces later as a query or a reassessment. Filing the schedules with nil amounts where they are required is what makes the year a filed nil year rather than an incomplete one.

No Audited Statements Are Needed

GIFI is not the same thing as financial statements. No audited or reviewed statements are needed for a nil T2, and none are prepared as part of this service.

What is filed is the GIFI schedules inside the return. See whether financial statements are needed for a nil T2 return.

How the Codes Work

Each line of the balance sheet and income statement carries a GIFI code: a four-digit number that tells the Canada Revenue Agency what the figure is. Cash has its own code, share capital has its own code, bank charges have their own.

Mapping a corporation’s own account names onto the right codes is the work in a nil GIFI filing, and it is what the CPA review checks before transmission.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a Nil Return Always Need GIFI Schedules?

No, but the exemption is narrow. A corporation inactive all year with nothing at all to report may omit Schedules 100, 125 and 141. Any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes them required.

Is GIFI the Same as Financial Statements?

No. GIFI is a code set used inside the T2 for the balance sheet and income statement. No audited or reviewed financial statements are needed for a nil return.

My Corporation Only Has Share Capital. Do I File GIFI?

Yes. Share capital of any amount is a balance on the books, and a balance is reported in every year it exists. This is the case owners most often get wrong.

What Does Schedule 141 Actually Ask?

Who prepared the financial information, whether an accountant was involved, and whether the statements were audited, reviewed or neither. For a nil return the answer is normally neither, which is accurate and expected.

Does Filing GIFI With Zeros Create Tax?

No. GIFI reports figures; it does not calculate tax. A true nil year reports nil net income and the corporation owes $0.00.

Are the GIFI Schedules Included in the Fee?

Yes, where they are required. The fee is $300.00 plus HST per tax year and covers Schedules 100, 125 and 141 along with the return itself.

Schedules Guide

The Complete Guide to Schedule 8 and Loss Continuity

What Schedule 8 records, how capital cost allowance works in a nil year, why loss continuity has to be carried forward, and what a skipped year costs. Nil T2 filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Schedule 8 Is

Schedule 8 is the capital cost allowance schedule. It records the corporation’s depreciable property, the class each asset sits in, and how much depreciation is claimed for the year.

A corporation with no depreciable property has no Schedule 8 to file. One that still holds equipment, a vehicle or a computer from its trading days does, even in a year when nothing happened.

Capital Cost Allowance in a Nil Year

Capital cost allowance is the tax version of depreciation. Each class of asset has a rate, and the undepreciated capital cost of the class is what remains to be claimed in future years.

Capital cost allowance is discretionary. A corporation may claim anything from nil up to the maximum the class allows, and the choice is made each year.

Claiming It or Leaving It

On a nil year the usual answer is to claim nil. Claiming capital cost allowance against no income creates a non-capital loss, and a non-capital loss expires. Leaving the claim unmade keeps the undepreciated capital cost in the pool, where it does not expire at all.

Choice in a nil yearWhat happens
Claim nil capital cost allowanceThe undepreciated capital cost stays in the pool for a future year
Claim the maximumA non-capital loss is created, which expires 20 years later

The Pools Carry Forward

Each class is a pool rather than a list of individual assets. The pool carries forward from year to year, reduced by what is claimed and by anything sold, and increased by anything bought.

That carry-forward is why the years are filed in order. A pool balance on one return is the opening balance on the next.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

What Loss Continuity Is

Loss continuity is the running record of the losses a corporation has and has not yet used. It is reported on Schedule 4, Corporation Loss Continuity and Application, not on Schedule 8.

The two are filed together and are often spoken of as one, but they are separate schedules. Schedule 8 is the asset pools; Schedule 4 is the losses.

How Long Losses Carry Forward

Type of lossCarry backCarry forward
Non-capital loss3 years20 years
Net capital loss3 yearsIndefinitely
Undepreciated capital cost in a poolNot applicableIndefinitely, while the pool exists

A non-capital loss is the ordinary kind, from expenses exceeding revenue. A net capital loss comes from selling capital property for less than it cost.

What a Skipped Year Does to the Continuity

A year that was never filed is a gap in the record. The losses and pools from the year before it have no filed return carrying them into the year after, so the continuity has to be rebuilt before the later years can be assessed correctly.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

On a true nil year the figures themselves are simple, which is what makes rebuilding the continuity straightforward rather than forensic.

Schedule 4 and Schedule 8 Together

ScheduleNameWhat it carries forward
Schedule 8Capital Cost AllowanceUndepreciated capital cost, by class
Schedule 4Corporation Loss Continuity and ApplicationNon-capital and net capital losses

Both are included in the fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year where the corporation has anything to record on them.

A Nil Year Is Not a Loss Year

These two are often confused. A nil year had no activity at all, so net income is nil and no loss arises. A loss year had real expenses exceeding real revenue, which creates a non-capital loss to carry forward.

A corporation that claims expenses is not nil, and this service is for a corporation with no activity in the tax year. A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Rebuilding Continuity on a Catch-Up

Where several years are outstanding, the pools and losses are carried through each return in turn. The earliest outstanding year is prepared first, its closing balances become the next year’s opening balances, and so on to the present.

The full sequence is in the guide to catching up on unfiled corporate tax returns.

Why the Years Are Filed Oldest First

Because continuity only runs forwards. A return filed out of order has opening balances that do not match the closing balances of the year before it, and that mismatch is what draws a query rather than a clean assessment.

It is the single practical reason the order matters on a multi-year filing.

CRA confirmationEmailed within 3 business days

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a Nil Return Need Schedule 8?

Only where the corporation holds depreciable property. A corporation with no assets of that kind has no Schedule 8 to file.

Should I Claim Capital Cost Allowance in a Nil Year?

Usually nil. Claiming against no income creates a non-capital loss that expires in 20 years, while claiming nothing keeps the undepreciated capital cost in the pool, where it does not expire.

Is Loss Continuity on Schedule 8?

No. Schedule 8 is capital cost allowance. Loss continuity is reported on Schedule 4, Corporation Loss Continuity and Application. The two are filed together, which is why they are often spoken of as one.

How Long Can a Non-Capital Loss Be Carried Forward?

Twenty years forward and three years back. A net capital loss carries forward indefinitely and back three years.

Does a Nil Year Create a Loss I Can Use Later?

No. A nil year had no activity, so net income is nil and no loss arises. A loss needs real expenses exceeding real revenue, and a corporation claiming expenses is not a nil filer.

What if an Unfiled Year Breaks the Continuity?

The gap is rebuilt by filing the missing years oldest first, so each return’s closing balances become the next one’s opening balances. On nil years the figures are simple enough that this is routine.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

When the First Tax Year Starts

On the incorporation date. Not on the day the first invoice goes out, not on the day the bank account opens, and not on the first of the following month.

This is the single most misunderstood point about a first return. A corporation registered in March and never traded still has a tax year that began in March, and a return due for it.

The 53-Week Rule

A corporation’s first tax year cannot exceed 53 weeks. That is the only hard limit on where the first year-end falls.

Within that window the date is the corporation’s own choice, which is why two corporations incorporated on the same day can have different year-ends and different due dates.

Choosing the First Year-End

ConsiderationEffect
Any date within 53 weeks of incorporationPermitted
A month-end rather than a mid-month dateSimpler to administer, no tax effect
A short first yearBrings the first filing deadline forward
A full 53-week first yearPushes the first filing deadline out
Changing it laterNeeds the Agency’s permission

Once the first return is filed, the year-end is set and later years run twelve months from it.

The Year-End the CRA Already Holds

The Canada Revenue Agency takes a year-end from the incorporation record and holds it before the corporation has filed anything. The first return has to carry that same date.

Where the owner intended a different year-end than the one on record, that is settled with the Agency before the return is transmitted, not by filing a different date and hoping.

One price for every year and every province. CPA reviewed and transmitted electronically.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Schedule 24, Required on a First Return

Schedule 24 is the first-time filer schedule, required on the first return after incorporation. It reports the corporation’s shareholders, its related corporations and how it came into existence.

It is filed once and not again. It is included in the fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

A First Year With No Trading

A corporation registered and then left unused has a nil first year, and a nil return is filed for it. Filing nothing is not an option the rules offer, and "we never started" is not a filing status.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

See whether a nil T2 is needed if the corporation never started operating.

Why First Transmissions Get Rejected

Because the year-end on the return does not match the one the Agency holds. It is the most common cause of a rejected first transmission, ahead of every other error combined.

CauseFix
Year-end taken from when trading startedUse the date on the incorporation record
Year-end more than 53 weeks after incorporationBring it inside the 53-week limit
Business number or RC account not yet activeConfirm the account before transmitting
Corporation name not matching the registryUse the exact legal name

One corrected transmission is included in the fee where the Agency rejects the first.

The Business Number and RC Account

The return is filed against the nine-digit business number and its RC corporation income tax account. Most corporations receive the number at incorporation, but it is confirmed as active before the first return goes out.

A corporation that never received one obtains it from the Canada Revenue Agency first.

GIFI on a First Return

A first-year corporation almost always has something on its balance sheet: the share capital issued on incorporation, and often the incorporation costs themselves.

That makes GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required on most first returns, even where the corporation never traded. The exemption for a corporation with nothing at all to report rarely applies in year one.

The detail is in the guide to GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141.

The First Filing Deadline

Six months after the first fiscal year-end, like every other year. A corporation incorporated in March with a December year-end has its first return due the following June.

Every fiscal year-end and its due date is listed on T2 filing deadlines.

A First Year That Was Never Filed

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

An unfiled first year is the one that compounds, because every later year sits on top of it and the Agency has no opening record for the corporation at all. Schedule 24 is still filed, late, on whichever return turns out to be the first one transmitted.

Frequently Asked Questions

When Does My First Tax Year Start?

On the incorporation date, not the day trading started. A corporation registered and never used still has a tax year running from the date on its incorporation record.

How Long Can My First Tax Year Be?

Up to 53 weeks. Within that window the year-end date is the corporation’s own choice, and it is fixed once the first return is filed.

Do I File a T2 if I Never Started the Business?

Yes. Incorporating creates the obligation. A corporation that never opened for business files a nil return rather than no return.

What Is Schedule 24?

The first-time filer schedule, required on the first return after incorporation. It reports shareholders, related corporations and how the corporation came into existence, and it is filed once.

Why Was My First Return Rejected?

Almost always a fiscal year-end that differs from the one the Canada Revenue Agency holds from the incorporation record. One corrected transmission is included in the fee.

Does a First-Year Nil Return Still Need GIFI?

Usually yes. Share capital issued on incorporation and capitalised incorporation costs both sit on the balance sheet, and either one makes Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required.

Numbered Company Guide

The Complete Guide to Numbered Company Tax Filing

Why a numbered company files exactly like a named one, how the CRA identifies it, what shelf and holding corporations need, and what the filing costs. Nil T2 filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOWNil T2 Filing Services

On this page

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What a Numbered Company Is

A corporation whose legal name is the number the registry assigned it, in the form 1234567 Ontario Inc. or 9876543 Canada Inc. Nothing was chosen; the registry issued a number and the corporation kept it.

Owners pick a numbered name to incorporate quickly, to avoid a name search, or because the corporation was never meant to trade under a name of its own.

The Obligation Is Identical

A numbered company is an ordinary corporation. It files a T2 within six months of each fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved, on exactly the same terms as a corporation with a chosen name.

There is no lighter regime for a numbered company, no different deadline and no different form. The numbered name affects nothing about the filing.

The CRA Identifies It by Business Number

The Canada Revenue Agency works from the nine-digit business number and its RC corporation income tax account, not from the corporate name. For filing purposes the name is a label on a record the number already identifies.

That is why a numbered company is no harder to file for. See whether a business number is needed to file a nil T2.

Shelf Corporations

A shelf corporation is one registered and then left unused, held in case it is wanted later. Most are numbered, because no name was needed for a corporation that was not going to trade.

A shelf corporation is the textbook nil filer: no revenue, no expenses, no payroll, a return every year reporting nil amounts. What it is not is exempt.

Nil T2 Filing, $300.00 plus HST per tax year

One price for every year and every province. CPA reviewed and transmitted electronically.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Numbered Holding Corporations Are Often Not Nil

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Many numbered corporations are holding companies, and a holding company earning investment income has no operations, no staff and no customers while still falling outside a nil return. The portfolio earns income that belongs on the return.

A numbered holding corporation that genuinely holds nothing and earns nothing is nil. One holding investments is not.

The Registry Record and the Annual Return

A numbered company files an annual return with its registry in exactly the way a named one does, confirming directors and the registered office. Filing the T2 does not satisfy it.

The full set is in the guide to provincial and federal annual returns.

Numbered Companies Are the Ones Most Often Forgotten

A numbered corporation has no brand, no website and no letterhead to remind anyone it exists. It generates no mail the owner recognises and appears on no invoice.

That is why unfiled years cluster on numbered companies. The obligation did not stop; the reminder did.

See whether nil T2 returns can be filed for a forgotten corporation.

Unfiled Years on a Numbered Company

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Each year is a separate return with its own fiscal year-end and its own due date. Filing several at once is routine and closes the years in a single pass; the sequence is in the guide to catching up on unfiled corporate tax returns.

Adding a Business Name Later

A numbered company can register a business name and trade under it while keeping the number as its legal name. The corporation does not change and neither does its business number.

The T2 is filed under the legal numbered name whatever the corporation trades as. A registered business name is a separate registry filing, not a change to the corporation.

Dissolving a Numbered Company

Identical to dissolving a named one. Every earlier year must already be filed, the final T2 is due within six months of the dissolution date, and a clearance certificate cannot be issued while any tax year is open.

Because a numbered company usually has no name worth keeping, dissolution is more often the right answer than it is for a named corporation. The sequence is in the guide to the final T2 and dissolution.

Deadlines

Six months after the fiscal year-end, every year. Where a due date falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday recognised by the Canada Revenue Agency, a return received the next business day is on time.

Every fiscal year-end and its due date is listed on T2 filing deadlines.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a Numbered Company File a Different Return?

No. It files the same T2, on the same deadline, with the same schedules. The numbered name affects nothing about the filing obligation.

How Does the CRA Know Which Corporation It Is?

By the nine-digit business number and its RC corporation income tax account. The corporate name is a label on a record the number already identifies.

Is a Shelf Corporation a Nil Filer?

Usually yes. A corporation registered and left unused has no revenue and no expenses, so it files a nil return every year until it is dissolved.

Is a Numbered Holding Company Nil?

Not where it earns investment income. A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil, and are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Can I Trade Under a Name Instead of the Number?

Yes, by registering a business name with the registry. The corporation and its business number do not change, and the T2 is still filed under the legal numbered name.

Why Do Numbered Companies End Up With Unfiled Years?

Because nothing reminds the owner they exist. No brand, no letterhead, no invoices. The filing obligation continues whether or not anything prompts it.
